title: Connecting Eulerian Numbers to Honest Permutations
content: The parent proved the closed form A(n,k) = ∑(−1)ⁱC(n+1,i)(k+1−i)ⁿ = ⟨n,k⟩ for the combinatorial Eulerian numbers, and asked (in its open question) to show that A(n,k) counts the permutations of {1,…,n} with exactly k descents. Siblings settled nonnegativity, row palindromy, and the descent moments analytically — but none of them defined the descent statistic on actual permutations. Mathlib has no permutation descent statistic (only Coxeter-group descents), so it must be built from scratch. This entry takes the first concrete step: it defines descentCount σ and proves the k = 0 base rung of the bijection — descent-free permutations are exactly the identity, counted by ⟨n+1,0⟩ = 1. This is the first place in the gallery where the abstract Eulerian number is matched against a genuine cardinality of a descent class. Columns k ≥ 1 (the full bijection via the insertion recurrence) remain open.
mathContext: $\langle n,k\rangle = \#\{\sigma \in S_n : \mathrm{des}(\sigma) = k\};$ this entry proves the $k=0$ rung $\langle n{+}1,0\rangle = 1$.

title: A Strictly Monotone Permutation Is the Identity
content: perm_eq_one_of_strictMono: a strictly monotone self-equivalence of Fin n must be the identity. The argument promotes σ to an order isomorphism: σ is monotone by hypothesis, and its inverse is monotone too (a short by_contra using strict monotonicity), so σ.toOrderIso gives an element of Fin n ≃o Fin n. That type is a subsingleton — a finite linear order has exactly one order automorphism, the identity — so Subsingleton.elim forces e = OrderIso.refl, hence σ i = i for all i. This is the structural lemma that pins down the unique descent-free permutation.
mathContext: $\sigma \in \mathrm{Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n) \text{ strictly monotone} \Rightarrow \sigma = \mathrm{id},$ since $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \simeq_o \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ is a subsingleton.
prerequisites: order isomorphisms on finite linear orders

title: The Descent Statistic
content: descentCount σ is defined as the number of positions i : Fin n where σ falls, i.e. σ(i.succ) < σ(i.castSucc) — the cardinality of the filter of descent positions among the n adjacent pairs of Fin (n+1). This is the permutation descent statistic des(σ), built directly since Mathlib lacks it. For n = 0 there are no adjacent pairs, so every permutation of Fin 1 is vacuously descent-free.

title: Descent-Free ⟺ Identity
content: descentCount_eq_zero_iff: a permutation of Fin (n+1) has zero descents exactly when it is the identity. Forward: zero descents means the descent filter is empty, so σ(i.castSucc) is never strictly above σ(i.succ); the strict inequality σ(i.castSucc) < σ(i.succ) follows by trichotomy — equality is impossible by injectivity (since castSucc < succ), and the reverse strict inequality is exactly the excluded descent. Strict monotonicity on adjacent pairs (Fin.strictMono_iff_lt_succ) then triggers perm_eq_one_of_strictMono, forcing σ = 1. Converse: the identity sends i.castSucc < i.succ, so it never descends and the descent filter is empty.

title: The Descent-Free Base Rung ⟨n+1,0⟩ = 1
content: card_descentFree: the descent-free permutations of Fin (n+1) number exactly the Eulerian number ⟨n+1,0⟩ = 1. Using eulerian_succ_zero (the left border of the Eulerian triangle is 1) and Finset.card_eq_one, the goal reduces to exhibiting a unique element of the descent-free class — which descentCount_eq_zero_iff identifies as the identity. This is the k = 0 case of the open claim |{σ : descentCount σ = k}| = ⟨n+1,k⟩, the first rung where the abstract Eulerian number is matched against an actual descent-class cardinality.
